## Wye Valley National Landscape

At the heart of the Wye Valley National Landscape flows the river Wye, which has created one of the finest lowland landscapes in Britain. The quality of this landscape was protected in 1971 when the lower Wye, south of Hereford, was designated an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

The Wye Valley National Landscape, designated as an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty in 1971, is one of Britain's finest lowland landscapes. The River Wye, flowing through this landscape, shapes its diverse scenery from softly rolling countryside in the north to dramatic limestone gorges downstream of Ross-on-Wye, including the famous Symonds Yat Rock.

The Wye Valley National Landscape is unique as it straddles both England and Wales, with the river marking the historical border between the two countries. Highlights include Goodrich Castle, perched high above the Wye, and the romantic ruins of Tintern Abbey, which have inspired artists and poets like Wordsworth and Turner. Piercefield, an outstanding example of an 18th-century picturesque landscape, was a must-see during the fashionable Wye Tour from Ross to Chepstow.

The Wye's significance for nature conservation is marked by its designation as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a Special Area of Conservation (SAC). However, recent issues like intensive poultry farming and climate change have impacted water quality, prompting restoration efforts. The Lower Wye Valley woodlands, also a SAC, are among Britain’s largest ancient woodlands, providing a refuge for rare species.

## Tirwedd Cenedlaethol Dyffryn Gwy

Tirwedd Cenedlaethol Dyffryn Gwy, a ddynodwyd yn Ardal o Harddwch Naturiol Eithriadol ym 1971, yw un o’r tirweddau iseldirol gorau ym Mhrydain. Mae Afon Gwy, sy’n llifo trwy’r dirwedd hon, yn ffurfio ei golygfeydd amrywiol o ardal wledig donnog ysgafn yn y gogledd i geunentydd calchfaen trawiadol i lawr yr afon o’r Rhosan ar Wy, gan gynnwys Craig Symonds Yat enwog.

Mae Tirwedd Cenedlaethol Dyffryn Gwy yn unigryw gan ei fod yng Nghymru a Lloegr, gyda’r afon yn nodi’r ffin hanesyddol rhwng y ddwy wlad. Mae uchafbwyntiau’n cynnwys Castell Goodrich, sy’n sefyll yn uchel uwchben Afon Gwy, ac adfeilion rhamantaidd Abaty Tintern, sydd wedi ysbrydoli artistiaid a beirdd fel Wordsworth a Turner. Roedd Piercefield, sy’n enghraifft ragorol o dirwedd darluniadwy o’r 18fed ganrif, yn olygfa yr oedd rhaid ei gweld yn ystod Taith ffasiynol Gwy o’r Rhosan i Gas-gwent.

Mae arwyddocâd Gwy i gadwraeth natur yn amlwg yn sgil ei dynodiad fel Safle o Ddiddordeb Gwyddonol Arbennig (SoDdGA) ac Ardal Cadwraeth Arbennig (ACA). Fodd bynnag, mae materion diweddar fel ffermio dofednod dwys a’r newid yn yr hinsawdd wedi effeithio ar ansawdd dŵr, gan ysgogi ymdrechion adfer. Mae coetiroedd Dyffryn Gwy Isaf, sydd hefyd yn ACA, ymhlith y coetiroedd hynafol mwyaf ym Mhrydain, sy’n darparu lloches i rywogaethau prin.

## The Wye Valley National Landscape

The Wye Valley National Landscape is a designated Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, looked after by a small team working in partnership with other organisations to conserve and enhance the natural beauty of the Wye Valley, to increase understanding and enjoyment of its special qualities and to foster the social and economic well-being of local communities.

**[Learn more](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/caring-for-wye-valley-aonb/)**

### Sign up to our newsletter

Subscribe to our newsletter for the latest news and events from the Wye Valley National Landscape Trust.

[Sign up](https://public.govdelivery.com/accounts/UKHEREF/subscriber/new?topic_id=UKHEREF_9191)

## Latest Projects & News

[**Wye Valley Walk 50th**](https://www.wyevalleywalk.org/)

[![](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/RUTH-LANDSCAPE-BOOK-FIN-67-insta-scaled.jpg)](https://www.wyevalleywalk.org/)

## Exploring the Wye Valley National Landscape

**How long do you have? Just an hour?** Then you won’t want to miss the romantic ruins of Tintern Abbey, in the prettiest of settings surrounded by river, trees and hills. **An afternoon?** Take a short boat trip along the Wye at Symonds Yat and then head up to Yat Rock to take in the Wye Valley’s most iconic view. **An evening to spare?** Make your way up the Kymin, near Monmouth, and savour the view as the sun sets over Monmouthshire’s stunning countryside. **All day?** Relax into a different pace of life, floating down the Wye in a canoe, and stopping for a leisurely lunch at a riverside pub. **A night time outing?** Head out at dusk to hear the amazing calls of nightjars on a summer’s evening on Beacon Hill near Trellech. **Or even ten days?** The Wye Valley Walk follows the River Wye for 136 miles from the source to sea, or vice versa.

[**Map of the AONB**![](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/Tintern-river-alamy-compressed-cta-1.jpg)](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/wye-valley-aonb-map/) [**Wye Valley Walk**![](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/walkers-heading-towards-Bigsweir-Bridge-on-english-side-of-river-gemma-wood-cta-2.jpg)](https://www.wyevalleywalk.org/) [**50 Walks @ 50**![](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/Wintours-leap-e1731494198670.png)](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/50-walks50/)

[**Explore on Foot**![Wye Valley On Foot](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/Wye-valley-walk-sign-on-foot.png)](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/exploring-wye-valley-aonb/wye-valley-on-foot/) [**Explore by Water**![Wye Valley On The Water](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/Wye-valley-walk-sign-on-water.png)](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/exploring-wye-valley-aonb/on-the-water/) [**Views and Picnic Sites**![the Wye Valley](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/About-AONBs-Symonds-yat-autumn-view-istock-500-by-500.jpg)](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/exploring-wye-valley-aonb/views-and-picnic/)

[**Explore the Landscape**![](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/Wye-Valley-Woodland-Gemma-Wood-1-e1691046676577.jpg)](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/exploring-wye-valley-aonb/landscape/) [**Explore the Wildlife**![](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/Peregrine-Wye-1-Wye-dean-tourism-association-credit-300-by-300.jpg)](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/exploring-wye-valley-aonb/wildlife/) [**Explore the Heritage**![Dan Cotterell Sun Star Through St James Church](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/Dan-Cotterell-Sun-Star-Through-St-James-Church-A-sm-e1646419534346.jpg)](https://www.wyevalley-nl.org.uk/exploring-wye-valley-aonb/heritage/)

# Symonds Yat Rock

## Visitor information

MTB - Stopwatch

Opening hours

Info

### Opening hours

Close

Symonds Yat Rock is open every day except Christmas Day. The site opens at 8am every day and the closing times are as follows:

- **November to February**– 5pm
- **March**– 6:30pm
- **April**– 8pm
- **May to August**– 9pm
- **September**– 7:30pm
- **October**– 6:30pm

Overnight parking is not permitted. The access barrier to the car park is locked at night when the site is closed.

Symonds Yat Rock doesn't have designated quiet times, but it is usually less busy on weekdays (outside of school holidays), earlier in the morning and later in the afternoon. If visiting at the weekend or on a bank holiday, the forest is usually less busy before 10am and after 4pm.

### Symonds Yat Rock Cafe

[Symonds Yat Rock Cafe's](https://www.forestryengland.uk/symonds-yat-rock/symonds-yat-rock-cafe) opening hours vary depending on the time of year.

### How to find us

Close

How to find us


What3Words location: [///prune.fells.brambles](https://w3w.co/prune.fells.brambles)

#### Sat Nav Postcode:

GL16 7NZ

near Coleford, Gloucestershire,
GLOUCESTER


#### By Car

Follow tourist signs for the Forest of Dean. Take the B4432 from Coleford and Christchurch, heading North. The site is on the left before the steep downhill road to the river.

Please note, if coming from the north along the B4229 from the Goodrich direction you will come up Yat Hill. This road is not suitable for larger vehicles.

#### By Public Transport

We welcome car-free visitors and those arriving by public transport or bike. See all public travel and active travel routes for the Forest of Dean District in the [Forest of Dean Travel Guide](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1onv9gklY0K4f4k77iKglKzxpgcgbbppQ/view).

#### OS Grid Ref

SO564160

[Get directions](https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&destination=51.83788064362,-2.6355895381287)

## 51.83788064362, -2.6355895381287

### Parking and prices

Close

You can pay for your parking at one of our parking machines with debit/credit card or Google Pay/Apple Pay. Equally, you can skip the queues and pay for your parking through the [RingGo app](https://ringgo.co.uk/).

**Please note:** Our car park pay machines are located in the main car park, next to the toilet block.

### Save with a membership

Forestry England members park for free at Symonds Yat Rock.

Support our work in the Forest of Dean with a [Forest of Dean membership](https://www.forestryengland.uk/the-forest-dean/forest-dean-membership), or choose a [national membership](https://www.forestryengland.uk/national-membership) and support the nation's forests. Both memberships cover the whole household.

### Parking Charges

The money you pay for parking helps us to look after the forests. [Read how](https://www.forestryengland.uk/parking)

## Symonds Yat Rock

## Experience the beauty of Symonds Yat Rock this autumn

Take in the sights of autumn at Symonds Yat Rock, an iconic viewpoint offering sweeping panoramic views of the River Wye and the surrounding landscape.

Whether you're a nature lover, history enthusiast or simply looking to enjoy the changing season, Symonds Yat Rock is the perfect place for an autumn day out.

### Discover and explore:

- Stand in awe as you take in the world‑renowned views, enhanced by the rich colours of the season – a perfect moment for photographers and nature spotters alike.
- Stop by our welcoming [log cabin cafe](https://www.forestryengland.uk/symonds-yat-rock/symonds-yat-rock-cafe) for a hot drink, light meal or seasonal treat.
- Choose your adventure with [waymarked walking trails](https://www.forestryengland.uk/symonds-yat-rock/walking-trails-symonds-yat-rock) leading down to the River Wye and across [Biblins Bridge](https://www.forestryengland.uk/biblins-bridge), or enjoy a walk beneath autumn foliage in the surrounding woodland.
- Little adventurers will love hunting for the hidden Gruffalo panels dotted around the woodland in our [Gruffalo orienteering](https://www.forestryengland.uk/symonds-yat-rock/gruffalo-orienteering-symonds-yat-rock) challenge.
- Step back in time and explore the intriguing ancient hill fort, surrounded by autumn colours and abundant wildlife.
- A dedicated [cycling trail](https://www.forestryengland.uk/symonds-yat-rock/symonds-yat-rock-cycle-trail) links Symonds Yat Rock with [Forest Holidays](https://www.forestryengland.uk/activities/forest-holidays) and [Bracelands Campsite](https://bracelandscamping.co.uk/), perfect for exploring on wheels while enjoying the longer, brighter days.
- A birdwatching haven, Symonds Yat Rock is one of the UK’s best spots for peregrine falcons. Autumn offers fantastic viewing opportunities, with the chance to spot goshawks, sparrowhawks, buzzards, ospreys, owls, ravens, and kestrels. Don't forget your binoculars.

### Ready to witness the wonder of Symonds Yat Rock?

For breathtaking views, incredible wildlife and refreshing walks in the height of summer, Symonds Yat Rock promises a memorable autumn day out.

### Quality from start to finish

Symonds Yat Rock is a quality assured visitor attraction, having been [quality assessed](https://www.ratedtrips.com/our-ratings/visitengland-quality-assessed-visitor-attractions-for-a-great-day-out) by VisitEngland. Their quality logo is more than a stamp of approval – it's an assurance that every aspect of your visit, from arrival to departure, has been independently checked to high standards.

Standing proudly atop a prominent hill, the Kymin and its nine acres of pleasure grounds, overlooks Monmouth and the beautiful Wye Valley.
Once part of the enormous Monmouthshire estate of the Duke of Beaufort, the Kymin’s fortunes have fluctuated over the last two centuries. Originally a popular picnic site in the late 18th century, building on the Round House commenced in 1794.
The Kymin is also home to the unusual Naval Temple. The Kymin Club arranged for the Naval Temple to be built with moneys raised between themselves and public subscription in 1800, it celebrates some of the greatest British admirals and victories of the time.
Today the Kymin is the perfect place to escape the hustle and bustle and enjoy a picnic against the stunning backdrop of the Wye Valley and the Brecon Beacons.
Though the Round House and Stables have recently been converted into Holiday Cottages and are no longer accessible to the public, the surrounding grounds remain open for everyone to enjoy.

National Trust car park. No toilets. Mobility parking - three accessible parking spaces, adjacent to the Round House, beyond the car park. Wheelchair accessible to The Roundhouse and the Naval Temple.
Three accessible parking spaces \| Tri lle parcio hygyrch
2 miles east of Monmouth and signposted off A4136. Please be aware that the road up to the Kymin is steep and winding with hairpin bends. Not suitable for coaches.

The Offa's Dyke long distance trail passes by The Kymin, stretching 177 miles along the beautiful Anglo/Welsh border.The Wysis Way also offers access to this property, running for 55 miles through the lovely, but very distinctive, areas of the Forest of Dean, Severn Vale and Cotswold.
A small group of visitors is standing in front of the white, two-storey, circular, castellated Georgian banqueting house at The Kymin, Monmouthshire, at sunset.

Standing proudly atop a prominent hill, the Kymin and its nine acres of pleasure grounds, overlooks Monmouth and the beautiful Wye Valley.
Once part of the enormous Monmouthshire estate of the Duke of Beaufort, the Kymin’s fortunes have fluctuated over the last two centuries. Originally a popular picnic site in the late 18th century, building on the Round House commenced in 1794.
The Kymin is also home to the unusual Naval Temple. The Kymin Club arranged for the Naval Temple to be built with moneys raised between themselves and public subscription in 1800, it celebrates some of the greatest British admirals and victories of the time.
Today the Kymin is the perfect place to escape the hustle and bustle and enjoy a picnic against the stunning backdrop of the Wye Valley and the Brecon Beacons.
Though the Round House and Stables have recently been converted into Holiday Cottages and are no longer accessible to the public, the surrounding grounds remain open for everyone to enjoy.

approved_stops.name: Tintern Abbey
approved_stops.quote: The Wye Valley National Landscape is unique as it straddles both England and Wales, with the river marking the historical border between the two countries. Highlights include Goodrich Castle, perched high above the Wye, and the romantic ruins of Tintern Abbey, which have inspired artists and poets like Wordsworth and Turner. Piercefield, an outstanding example of an 18th-century picturesque landscape, was a must-see during the fashionable Wye Tour from Ross to Chepstow.

approved_stops.name: Symonds Yat Rock
approved_stops.quote: The Wye Valley National Landscape, designated as an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty in 1971, is one of Britain's finest lowland landscapes. The River Wye, flowing through this landscape, shapes its diverse scenery from softly rolling countryside in the north to dramatic limestone gorges downstream of Ross-on-Wye, including the famous Symonds Yat Rock.

approved_stops.name: Kymin
approved_stops.quote: **How long do you have? Just an hour?** Then you won’t want to miss the romantic ruins of Tintern Abbey, in the prettiest of settings surrounded by river, trees and hills. **An afternoon?** Take a short boat trip along the Wye at Symonds Yat and then head up to Yat Rock to take in the Wye Valley’s most iconic view. **An evening to spare?** Make your way up the Kymin, near Monmouth, and savour the view as the sun sets over Monmouthshire’s stunning countryside. **All day?** Relax into a different pace of life, floating down the Wye in a canoe, and stopping for a leisurely lunch at a riverside pub. **A night time outing?** Head out at dusk to hear the amazing calls of nightjars on a summer’s evening on Beacon Hill near Trellech. **Or even ten days?** The Wye Valley Walk follows the River Wye for 136 miles from the source to sea, or vice versa.
